text:
A: Hiya, can you hear me? I'm Craig, I'm in Warrington.
B: Mate! I'm Joel, I'm from Warrington. Well, Manchester now, Levenshulme, but Great Sankey originally.
A: Great Sankey? That's where I live! I saw the Wolves shirt in your photo and I thought, he's one of ours.
B: Made up. And I saw the magnet on your fridge. Gemma said she'd had a fella from Warrington with a Wolves magnet and a cockapoo called Biscuit, so I knew it was you.
A: (laughs) The famous Biscuit. Turns out there's three of them in this study. Which bit of Great Sankey were you?
B: Near the leisure centre. My mum and dad are still there, I'm back most fortnights for Sunday dinner at my nan's.
A: You'll have driven past mine, then. Small world. Do you get to the Halliwell Jones much?
B: Handful of times a season, with my dad. Easter was grim, wasn't it.
A: Don't. Losing to Saints at Easter, I couldn't speak to anyone for two days. Kerry said I was mardy all weekend.
B: (laughs) My dad was the same. So what do you do?
A: Sales, commercial flooring. Carpet tiles, vinyl, offices, schools, care homes, all round Cheshire, Merseyside and Manchester. You?
B: Solicitor. Corporate, in town, mostly people selling businesses, share purchases, that sort of thing. My dad still asks when I'm getting a proper trade, he's a plumber.
A: (laughs) That's very Warrington, that. You'll have clients like mine, then, blokes who've run a firm thirty years.
B: Exactly that. Half of it's just them being nervous and wanting someone to talk to, you know. I had a completion go till midnight Tuesday, and I've still not recovered. Bacon barm the next morning was the only thing that got me through.
A: Sausage barm for me, on site. Regretted it every time. Do you play anything?
B: Five-a-side, Wednesday nights, cage pitch in Longsight. When deals allow, which is never. It got rained off last week anyway.
A: Wednesday! Me too. Well, I say play. Dodgy ankle, I'm more of a, you know, a presence.
B: (laughs) A presence. I'll use that. I do parkrun Saturdays as well, Platt Fields, when I'm not hungover.
A: Fair play. I've taken up golf, partly for clients, if I'm honest. Twenty-four handicap and happy there.
B: That's smart, to be fair. We've got partners at work who do the whole golf day thing and I just sort of nod along.
A: Get yourself a set, mate, best networking going. Do you think you'll stay in Manchester?
B: Probably. Looking to buy with my girlfriend in a couple of years, Stockport or Heaton Moor maybe. Not Warrington, don't tell my mum.
A: Your secret's safe. I'll tell her I've never met you.
